question:
Two isotopes of hydrogen are used: protium ($^1\mathrm{H}$, nuclear mass $M_p=m_p$) and deuterium ($^2\mathrm{H}$, nuclear mass $M_d=m_d$). The reduced-mass corrected Rydberg constant is

$$R(M)=\frac{R_\infty}{1+\frac{m_e}{M}}.$$

For each isotope, two Balmer lines are measured:

- Line (I): $3\to 2$ with wavelength $\lambda_{32}$.
- Line (II): $4\to 2$ with wavelength $\lambda_{42}$.

The measured isotope shifts (protium minus deuterium) are

$$\Delta\lambda_{32}=\lambda_{32}(^1\mathrm{H})-\lambda_{32}(^2\mathrm{H})=0.180\,\text{nm},$$
$$\Delta\lambda_{42}=\lambda_{42}(^1\mathrm{H})-\lambda_{42}(^2\mathrm{H})=0.133\,\text{nm}.$$

Assume point nuclei and ignore fine structure. Using only the Rydberg formula

$$\frac{1}{\lambda}=R(M)\left(\frac{1}{n_f^2}-\frac{1}{n_i^2}\right),$$

determine whether these two measured shifts are mutually consistent with the reduced-mass model to first order.

You may use $\lambda_{32}\approx 656\,\text{nm}$ and $\lambda_{42}\approx 486\,\text{nm}$.

options.A: Yes. The reduced-mass model predicts $\dfrac{\Delta\lambda_{32}}{\Delta\lambda_{42}}\approx \left(\dfrac{\lambda_{32}}{\lambda_{42}}\right)^2$, and the given data satisfy this.
options.B: Yes. The reduced-mass model predicts $\dfrac{\Delta\lambda_{32}}{\Delta\lambda_{42}}\approx \dfrac{\lambda_{32}}{\lambda_{42}}$, and the given data satisfy this.
options.C: No. The reduced-mass model predicts $\Delta\lambda_{32}=\Delta\lambda_{42}$, independent of transition.
options.D: No. The reduced-mass model predicts $\dfrac{\Delta\lambda_{32}}{\Delta\lambda_{42}}\approx \left(\dfrac{\lambda_{42}}{\lambda_{32}}\right)^2$, which the given data contradict.
